questions: How many direct reports would you have in the first six months, and do you decide who is hired and how they are paid?
Can your manager give you a written timeline or promotion criteria for a lead role?
Will the startup's team lead role include one-on-ones, performance reviews and growth plans for others, or mostly coding?
How many months can the household pay the mortgage and living costs from savings if the startup paid you nothing?
If you leave and it goes badly, can you return to your current company, and is there any rehire policy?
Could you ask your current company for a different route, such as a tech lead role, mentoring or a temporary lead assignment?
Does your company usually fill lead roles by promoting from inside, and how long did it take those people?
How many months of salary payments does the startup's current cash cover at its present spending, and is a new funding round in progress?
Has anyone at your company recently been promoted to lead despite the hiring freeze, and how?
Is there a deadline on the offer, and can it be extended while you collect answers?

criteria: Realistic route to an engineering manager role within 3 years, including whether the role involves actual people management and growth
Household can pay the mortgage on one income through a downside scenario (startup shutting down or delayed salary) with a defined runway
Total compensation including realistic equity value, benefits and severance compared with the current role
The role gives credible management experience that transfers if the startup fails
stated_facts: Offer: team lead at a 40-person startup with +15% base salary, equity, and title Team Lead
Current role: senior engineer at a large company, stable employer
Goal: engineering manager within 3 years, with enough financial stability to pay a mortgage
Mortgage payments and a one-income household
Startup raised a seed round two years ago and is growing
Founders want the user to build the backend team
Current company has had a hiring freeze for a year; manager says a lead position may open 'at some point'

assumptions.text: The startup's team lead role will count as and lead toward engineering management, rather than being a senior individual contributor role with a lead title.
The startup will survive and keep paying salaries for at least as long as the mortgage risk requires.
A lead role at the current company is unlikely, given the hiring freeze and vague wording.
The equity will have meaningful value.
Management experience at a 40-person startup will be recognised by later employers as a step toward engineering manager.

uncertainties.text: What is the startup's runway and funding status: when does the seed money run out, what are revenue and burn, and is a next round in sight?
uncertainties.if_resolved: If there are 18+ months of runway or revenue covering costs, the offer is less risky and favors accepting; if runway is under about a year with no round in view, a one-income mortgage household is exposed and staying is favored.

uncertainties.text: What would the team lead role really involve: hiring authority, direct reports, budget, headcount plan, and time split between management and coding?
uncertainties.if_resolved: If the role has real hiring and people responsibility, it directly serves the manager goal and favors the offer; if it is mostly hands-on coding, it adds less toward management and weakens the case.

uncertainties.text: What is the true concrete chance and timing of a lead role at the current company, and can the manager commit to criteria or a date?
uncertainties.if_resolved: If a written path or date exists within about a year, staying is favored; if it stays vague amid the freeze, the offer's path advantage grows.

uncertainties.text: What do the equity terms say: type, strike price, vesting schedule, cliff, valuation, dilution, and what happens on exit or leaving?
uncertainties.if_resolved: If terms are fair and valuation plausible, equity adds upside favoring the offer; if heavily diluted or illiquid, it should be valued near zero and the 15% base alone decides.

uncertainties.text: What are the full compensation and benefits differences: bonus, pension, health, parental or sick leave, notice and severance terms, and how does the net compare for mortgage purposes?
uncertainties.if_resolved: If the startup's total package is equal or better, it favors the offer; if the large company's benefits and bonus outweigh the 15%, staying is favored.

uncertainties.text: How much cash buffer does the household hold, and how does the mortgage (fixed or variable, lender's view of a new employer or probation period) interact with changing jobs?
uncertainties.if_resolved: If there is a buffer covering 6+ months and the lender and mortgage terms are unaffected, the startup's risk is manageable and favors the offer; if the buffer is thin or a probation period creates problems, staying is favored.

uncertainties.text: How easy would it be to return to a similar senior role at a large company if the startup fails, and would the lead title help?
uncertainties.if_resolved: If the market for the user's skills is strong, downside is limited, favoring the offer; if re-entry is slow, staying is favored.

chosen.question: How many direct reports would you have in the first six months, and do you decide who is hired and how they are paid?
chosen.why: Real hiring and people responsibility favors the offer for your management goal.
chosen.answer_path: Ask the founders for the hiring plan, headcount budget and decision rights, and ask to see them in writing.

chosen.question: Can your manager give you a written timeline or promotion criteria for a lead role?
chosen.why: A written path within a year would make staying stronger.
chosen.answer_path: Ask your manager, and your manager's manager or HR, for specific criteria and dates.

chosen.question: Will the startup's team lead role include one-on-ones, performance reviews and growth plans for others, or mostly coding?
chosen.why: Checks whether the lead title means real management.
chosen.answer_path: Ask the founders for a sample week and the expected time split, and talk to someone who has held the role.

chosen.question: How many months can the household pay the mortgage and living costs from savings if the startup paid you nothing?
chosen.why: Sets the point at which the startup risk becomes unaffordable.
chosen.answer_path: Add monthly costs and divide your cash savings by that, excluding retirement accounts.

chosen.question: If you leave and it goes badly, can you return to your current company, and is there any rehire policy?
chosen.answer_path: Ask HR about rehire policies and ask colleagues who left and returned.

chosen.question: Could you ask your current company for a different route, such as a tech lead role, mentoring or a temporary lead assignment?
chosen.why: Adds ways to gain management experience at your current employer.
chosen.answer_path: Ask your manager about acting lead or project lead responsibilities.

chosen.question: Does your company usually fill lead roles by promoting from inside, and how long did it take those people?
chosen.why: Tests whether waiting at your company leads to a lead role.
chosen.answer_path: Look at how recent leads were chosen and how long each waited.

chosen.question: How many months of salary payments does the startup's current cash cover at its present spending, and is a new funding round in progress?
chosen.why: Short runway with no round makes staying clearly safer for a one-income mortgage household.
chosen.answer_path: Ask the founders for cash balance, monthly burn, revenue and investor conversations; ask to speak with an investor or advisor.

chosen.question: Has anyone at your company recently been promoted to lead despite the hiring freeze, and how?
chosen.why: Checks whether a lead role at your employer is as unlikely as assumed.
chosen.answer_path: Review internal promotions of the last year and ask colleagues.

chosen.question: Is there a deadline on the offer, and can it be extended while you collect answers?
chosen.why: Shows how long you have to learn more.
chosen.answer_path: Ask the founders for the date and whether more time is possible.

candidates.question: How many months of salary payments does the startup's current cash cover at its present spending, and is a new funding round in progress?
candidates.why: Short runway with no round makes staying clearly safer for a one-income mortgage household.
candidates.answer_path: Ask the founders for cash balance, monthly burn, revenue and investor conversations; ask to speak with an investor or advisor.

candidates.question: How many direct reports would you have in the first six months, and do you decide who is hired and how they are paid?
candidates.why: Real hiring and people responsibility favors the offer for your management goal.
candidates.answer_path: Ask the founders for the hiring plan, headcount budget and decision rights, and ask to see them in writing.

candidates.question: Can your manager give you a written timeline or promotion criteria for a lead role?
candidates.why: A written path within a year would make staying stronger.
candidates.answer_path: Ask your manager, and your manager's manager or HR, for specific criteria and dates.

candidates.question: After bonus, pension, health, leave and notice terms are counted, is the startup's package higher or lower than your current one?
candidates.why: The 15% base may not tell the full difference.
candidates.answer_path: Put both offers in a spreadsheet using the offer letter and your current benefits documents.

candidates.question: If the startup failed after a year, how quickly could you get a senior engineer job at a large company?
candidates.why: Easy re-entry reduces the downside of leaving.
candidates.answer_path: Check current openings and ask recruiters or peers who left for startups.

candidates.question: Will the startup's team lead role include one-on-ones, performance reviews and growth plans for others, or mostly coding?
candidates.why: Checks whether the lead title means real management.
candidates.answer_path: Ask the founders for a sample week and the expected time split, and talk to someone who has held the role.

candidates.question: What do current employees and recent leavers say about whether salaries have been paid on time?
candidates.why: Checks whether the startup will keep paying.
candidates.answer_path: Speak to two or three current or former engineers, away from the founders.

candidates.question: Has anyone at your company recently been promoted to lead despite the hiring freeze, and how?
candidates.why: Checks whether a lead role at your employer is as unlikely as assumed.
candidates.answer_path: Review internal promotions of the last year and ask colleagues.

candidates.question: What do you expect the equity to be worth, and what is that based on?
candidates.why: Checks whether equity should count for anything.
candidates.answer_path: Ask for the cap table share, latest valuation and preference terms, and model several outcomes.

candidates.question: Would the managers hiring engineering managers at your target employers count a lead role at a 40-person startup toward the requirement?
candidates.why: Checks whether the experience transfers.
candidates.answer_path: Ask engineering managers or recruiters, and compare job requirements.

candidates.question: Have previous people with this title at the startup moved into manager roles, there or elsewhere?
candidates.why: Tests whether the role leads to management in practice.
candidates.answer_path: Ask the founders and check LinkedIn for past leads.

candidates.question: Does your company usually fill lead roles by promoting from inside, and how long did it take those people?
candidates.why: Tests whether waiting at your company leads to a lead role.
candidates.answer_path: Look at how recent leads were chosen and how long each waited.

candidates.question: Does the startup's growth show up in revenue or customers, or only in headcount and funding?
candidates.why: Tests whether growth means a sustainable business.
candidates.answer_path: Ask for revenue and customer trends over the last four quarters.

candidates.question: If the startup were sold or shut down within three years, what would your vested shares yield, given the preference terms?
candidates.why: Tests whether equity pays out in realistic outcomes.
candidates.answer_path: Request the equity documents and have an advisor or lawyer model outcomes.

candidates.question: Does your mortgage lender need your employer or probation status for any changes, such as refinancing?
candidates.why: Tests whether changing jobs affects your mortgage.
candidates.answer_path: Call the lender and check mortgage terms and any upcoming refinance date.

candidates.question: How many months can the household pay the mortgage and living costs from savings if the startup paid you nothing?
candidates.why: Sets the point at which the startup risk becomes unaffordable.
candidates.answer_path: Add monthly costs and divide your cash savings by that, excluding retirement accounts.

candidates.question: At what level of runway would you decline the offer?
candidates.why: Sets a limit that turns the facts into a decision.
candidates.answer_path: Decide a minimum number of months, then ask the founders for figures to compare.

candidates.question: How large could the backend team grow before the startup needs a manager above you, and would you be that person?
candidates.why: Finds the point where the role's management path stops or grows.
candidates.answer_path: Ask the founders for the hiring plan for the next two years and the org structure.

candidates.question: If your salary were delayed by two months, what bills would first become a problem?
candidates.why: Finds the limit of tolerance for delayed pay.
candidates.answer_path: Review your monthly budget and fixed commitments.

candidates.question: How much longer than a year would you wait at your company before the lack of a lead role makes staying a poor choice?
candidates.why: Sets your time limit for staying.
candidates.answer_path: Decide your own deadline against the three-year goal and tell your manager.

candidates.question: Could you get a lead or management role at a different mid-sized company that is hiring, instead of these two options?
candidates.why: The map only covers two options.
candidates.answer_path: Search openings and talk with recruiters for lead roles at mid-size firms.

candidates.question: Could you ask your current company for a different route, such as a tech lead role, mentoring or a temporary lead assignment?
candidates.why: Adds ways to gain management experience at your current employer.
candidates.answer_path: Ask your manager about acting lead or project lead responsibilities.

candidates.question: How would you negotiate the startup offer, for example a higher salary, a title with direct reports or a severance clause?
candidates.why: The terms might be improved.
candidates.answer_path: List what you would ask for and raise it with the founders.

candidates.question: What do you think of working with these founders: their management style, how they treat engineers and how they make decisions?
candidates.why: The map lacks working relationship with the founders.
candidates.answer_path: Spend time with the founders, ask for references and talk to the engineers.

candidates.question: Does your household have other ways to cover risk, such as a partner's skills or the ability to cut costs?
candidates.why: Household resilience affects how much startup risk is workable.
candidates.answer_path: Discuss with your household and list the options and what each would cost.

candidates.question: Is there a deadline on the offer, and can it be extended while you collect answers?
candidates.why: Shows how long you have to learn more.
candidates.answer_path: Ask the founders for the date and whether more time is possible.

candidates.question: If you decline now, would the startup or a similar role still be available in six months?
candidates.why: Shows what waiting costs.
candidates.answer_path: Ask the founders directly how long the role stays open.

candidates.question: If you leave and it goes badly, can you return to your current company, and is there any rehire policy?
candidates.why: Shows how reversible leaving is.
candidates.answer_path: Ask HR about rehire policies and ask colleagues who left and returned.

candidates.question: What do you forfeit by leaving, such as unvested stock, bonus or other benefits at your current company?
candidates.why: Identifies what you cannot get back.
candidates.answer_path: Check your current compensation documents for vesting and bonus timing.

candidates.question: What is your impression that the startup is growing based on: what the founders said, or numbers you have seen?
candidates.why: Separates claims from figures.
candidates.answer_path: List what you have been told versus what has been shown in documents.

candidates.question: What is your belief that a lead role will not open at your company based on?
candidates.why: Checks whether the estimate rests on evidence or on the vague wording.
candidates.answer_path: Ask yourself what examples you have seen, and check with your manager.

candidates.question: How did you come to your view of what the equity might be worth, and who told you?
candidates.why: Checks the source of the equity estimate.
candidates.answer_path: Trace the figure to a document or ask an independent advisor.

candidates.question: Is your view that startup management experience will count based on people you know who made the move, or on hope?
candidates.why: Checks the basis of the transfer assumption.
candidates.answer_path: Find three real examples and look at their paths.
